newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MARSEILLE PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF MARSEILLE PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to turn out for Marseille against Auxerre in the French first division match at the Velodrome stadium on Sunday:

Andreas Koepke, goalkeeper, age 33. A member of Germany's European championship-winning side this year, he has been a tower of strength during a troublesome settling-in period for Marseille in their first season back in the top flight. He joined the club after his transfer to Barcelona fell through.

Jerome Alonzo, goalkeeper, 24. Promotion side's goalkeeper, he is now Koepke's reserve. He played in his side's midweek League Cup win over Auxerre and could play if the German fails to prove his fitness after World Cup duty with his country on Saturday.

Christophe Galtier, defender, 30. Former French under-21 international who returned to Marseille, his first club, in 1995 after playing for Lille, Toulouse, Angers and Nimes. Played in Marseille's 1986 and 1987 French Cup final sides.

Ivan Franceschini, defender, 20. A tall (1.88 metres), young Italian (turned 20 last weekend) who joined from Parma this season without any first team action in Serie A. He has had mixed fortunes, having been sent off twice already as Marseille have accumulated 10 red cards.

Chris Makin, defender, 23. Englishman who joined Marseille from Oldham Athletic this season as a second string player but has benefited from numerous suspensions picked up by team mates and played in 13 matches.
Hamada Jambay, defender, 21. Born in the Comoros Islands, he rose through the club's youth ranks after joining at the age of eight. A first team regular for two seasons.
Alberto Malusci, defender, 24. Signed from Fiorentina after helping them win the Italian Cup last season. Looked on his way to AC Milan at one time but was out for a long period due to injury.

Jean-Philippe Durand, midfielder, 36. The only remaining player from the club's glory days in the early 1990s, having joined club from Bordeaux in 1991. He is playing his last season before retiring. Auxerre were the rivals in his first division debut for Toulouse in 1983. Won 26 caps for France.
Eric Roy, midfielder, 29. Signed from Lyon this season to help strengthen team promoted from the second division. He has been one of the steadiest new players and contributed three goals.
Olivier Echouafni, midfielder, 24. Began his career at Monaco. Dubbed the "washing machine" by coach Gerard Gili for his capacity to recycle Marseille's midfield play.

Yordan Lechkov, midfielder, 29. Bulgarian international who reached heights by helping his country to the 1994 World Cup semifinals, but subsequently lost his form at Marseille. Has begun to make a comeback as substitute.
Ludovic Assuar, midfielder, 20. Local boy, French under-21 international who turned 20 in October and has won extended run in the first team since Lechkov fell out of favour with coach Gerard Gili.

Reynald Pedros, midfielder, 25. Joined this season from 1995 champions Nantes. A current French international, he is very skilled but his commitment was questioned during an early season slump. Has helped the club get back on track and scored his first Marseille goal in their League Cup win over Auxerre on Tuesday.
Medhi Ben Slimane, forward, 22. Tunisian international who has been plagued by injuries this season, but could play.

Xavier Gravelaine, forward, 28. Capped four times by France, much-travelled striker who joined from Guingamp this season after two spells with Paris St-Germain and was made captain. Like, Pedros, his commitment was called into question by fans, but he has helped the side's recent recovery. Club's top scorer with five goals.
Marc Libbra, forward, 24. Scored 14 goals (second only to Irishman Tony Cascarino's 30) during promotion season.
